extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom leaders, journalism students, and people interested in journalism ethics
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and cautionary lessons for journalists and newsrooms about preventing ethical lapses (plagiarism, fabrication) under resource constraints, drawn from Jayson Blair's experience and remarks to a fellowship audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper attribution and sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must include proper attribution and not 'lift' material from wire services or other reporting without credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blair recalled 'lifting information for a story related to the attacks from the Associated Press at the time without including proper attribution.' Ensure clear sourcing and attribution for borrowed facts or phrasing to avoid plagiarism allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fabrication and plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting must not include invented facts or plagiarized material; fabrication and plagiarism constitute serious journalistic malpractice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece references Blair's 'multiple incidents of plagiarism and fabrication' that led to his resignation. Maintain rigorous verification of facts and do not create or misrepresent sources or events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain personal integrity and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual character and integrity are central; journalists must accept responsibility for errors and ethical choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blair: 'I really do believe I’m responsible for what I did… lack of integrity played a huge role in it for me.' Cultivate ethical habits, own mistakes, and avoid rationalizing small compromises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve newsroom guardrails (verification, editing, fact-checking, oversight)
rubrics_metrics.description: News organizations should keep institutional safeguards—editors, fact-checkers, verification processes—that prevent ethical lapses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title and argument: 'Removing Newsroom Guardrails Invites Ethical Lapses.' The article warns that persistent layoffs and declining resources weaken these safeguards; newsrooms must protect processes that catch errors and misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match expectations to available resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial expectations and workloads should be realistic given staffing and resource levels to avoid pressuring reporters into cutting ethical corners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blair notes 'the same expectations we did, and less support'—shrinking operations with unchanged expectations increase risk. Adjust assignments, deadlines, and scope to what the newsroom can responsibly support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support journalists' mental health and wellbeing
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsrooms and journalists must attend to mental health—providing support, accommodations, and resources—to reduce risk of errors tied to illness or burnout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blair urged journalists to 'care for their mental well-being' and acknowledged his bipolar diagnosis accelerated his decline. Offer mental-health resources, coaching, and reduce stigma around seeking help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide training, mentorship, and career support
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations should offer training, mentorship, and career/mental-health coaching so reporters can manage pressures ethically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: Blair is now a managing partner of a consulting firm specializing in career and mental health coaching and spoke to a fellowship audience. Invest in professional development and mentorship to reinforce ethical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and resist incremental compromises
rubrics_metrics.description: Be vigilant about 'little moments' of compromise because small ethical concessions can accumulate into major misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blair: 'It’s presented in little moments where you make little compromises.' Establish norms and checks to catch and correct small lapses before they escalate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage stress and develop coping strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters should have practices and institutional supports to manage stress so pressure does not lead to cutting corners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blair asked, 'How do you function in this environment... And so how do you manage the stress?' Encourage workload management, time for reflection, peer support, and access to counseling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency, corrections, and institutional accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: When ethical failures occur, outlets must correct the record, be transparent about errors, and hold people and processes accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page links to 'CORRECTING THE RECORD; Times Reporter Who Resigned Leaves Long Trail of Deception' and describes Blair's contrition—newsrooms should promptly correct errors and explain failures to retain public trust.
